newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Workers and students battle police in Seoul streets.
newsitem.headline: Workers and students battle police in Seoul streets.

text.p: Up to 15,000 workers and students clashed violently with riot police in central Seoul on Wednesday as they tried to march on a cathedral where trade union leaders are seeking sanctuary from arrest, witnesses said.
Riot police fired volleys of tear gas at the protesters, who fought back with iron bars and rocks.
There were no reports of any arrests from the clash, the first major street battle between police and protesters on a day unions had threatened the biggest strike in the country's history.
Witnesses said the clash erupted after riot police blocked the path of the workers and students near Myongdong Cathedral.

Prosecutors have threatened seven leaders from the outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions with imminent arrest for plotting three weeks of stoppages in protest at a labour law rammed through parliament on December 26.
Union calls for nationwide strikes on Tuesday and Wednesday have been largely ignored.
